summary:
EarthSense is an interactive web application that uses NISAR radar observations to make Earth’s surface changes easier to visualize, understand, and communicate. We developed a global exploration map, tools for comparing radar observations, and an educational flood preparedness game, available in Spanish and English.

Our application addresses the challenge by focusing on wetlands and water-related landscape changes. Users can explore locations worldwide and examine a prepared comparison of official NISAR visualizations from NASA GIBS for the Ozama Wetlands in the Dominican Republic. An advanced workflow compares compatible user-imported NISAR GCOV layers from two dates, displaying increases and decreases in radar backscatter. Sentinel-2 imagery provides complementary information about classified open water.
details:
EarthSense / The Pulse of the Earth

EarthSense is an interactive educational platform designed to help people understand changes in the Earth's surface through satellite data and visual analysis tools.

Inspired by the devastating floods in the Dominican Republic in November 2023, our project aims to make scientific information more accessible and raise awareness about environmental risks.

Users can explore different regions, compare satellite information from different dates, and identify changes in land and water. EarthSense also includes an educational game that teaches flood safety and preparedness.

Our mission is to connect science, technology, and education to help communities better understand and protect our planet.

Because the planet has a heartbeat… and we want to learn to listen to it!
Main Features

  • Interactive Map: Explore different regions of the world and learn how the Earth's surface changes.
  • Satellite Exploration: Observe satellite information and understand how technology helps us study our planet.
  • Environmental Analysis: Compare data from different dates to identify changes in land and water.
  • Educational Flood Game: Learn how to recognize flood risks and make safer decisions through interactive challenges.
    ABOUT THE GAME:
    Escape the Flood is an educational adventure in a fictional block world near the Ozama Wetlands. Prepare an emergency kit, avoid obstacles, and help two neighbors reach safety before the flood catches you.
  • Level 1.1 — Prepare Your Backpack: Explore six rooms and collect six emergency supplies in 30 seconds: drinking water, a flashlight and batteries, a first aid kit, a radio, protected documents, and a manual can opener.
  • Level 1.2 — Choose Safe Food: Inspect seven food items in 75 seconds. Check expiration dates, packaging, and refrigeration requirements. Pack the three suitable options and leave the others behind. Incorrect decisions add a five-second penalty.
  • Level 2 — Reach Safety: Leave the house and follow the route to the green flag. You have three hearts; puddles and debris cost one heart per hit. Losing all hearts restarts the route with the flood closer. If the flood reaches you, you return to Level 1 with the supplies moved to different rooms.
  • Level 3 — Rescue and Escape: Find Ana and Luis, accompany them to the car, and follow the winding road. Stop at the gas station, turn off the engine to refuel, then drive everyone to the safe exit. The flood keeps advancing while you refuel!

After completing the adventure, review your time and answer four short safety questions. You can customize your character, use practice mode, and pause the game.

The game teaches emergency preparedness. In a real emergency, evacuate early, follow official instructions, and never walk or drive through floodwater.
EarthSense serves different audiences through two connected experiences. The game is designed especially for children, who are among the most vulnerable groups during floods. Through interactive challenges, it introduces emergency preparedness, safe decision-making, and helping others in an engaging, age-appropriate way.

The interactive map is designed for everyone. It allows students, educators, families, and the wider public to explore the Earth, compare satellite observations, and better understand changes in water and landscapes.
EarthSense connects observation with preparation. Our map makes satellite observations accessible to everyone, while our game turns flood preparedness into an experience children can explore and practice. We want young learners to recognize unsafe choices, understand why preparation matters, and bring those conversations home to their families.
“Seeing a changing planet is only the beginning. Learning how to respond is what makes that knowledge matter.”
